events.note: Eight contestants step into the Glass Bridge.

events.text: The game has just begun, and I need to establish a good position. Moving to the front is risky as the person at the front takes the first risk on the bridge. However, the prizes are for 1st, 2nd, and 3rd, so being at the front could lead to a better prize if I survive. I should c

events.name: Fenn

events.name: Hana

events.name: Dara
events.text: Row 6 safe is L. Bex is front and must choose. I should publicly share row 6 to save Bex and keep alliance. No need to whisper now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Row 6 safe is L. Trust this one.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm not at the front, so I can only wait. Bex is at the front and needs to make a decision.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex, be cautious, we still don't know the pattern.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm fourth in line with no decision this row. Only the front agent risks elimination, so I just wait and watch what the next reveals show.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 6 confirmed R weak, as I predicted for 4+. My pattern: 1-3 L weak, 4-8 R weak has been perfect so far. Row 7 should be R weak, so safe is L. My anchor power protects me anyway, but I'll prove the pattern.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Five alive, two rows left. If Bex picks safe both rows, all five of us survive the bridge. Being last in line is safest, so I'll wait and urge Bex to pick carefully. Pattern so far suggests R weak in recent rows; I'll nudge toward L without claiming knowledge.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex, rows 4-6 were R-weak. If the pattern flips or holds, think hard — if you pick right we ALL survive this bridge.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Only 2 rows left. Row 7 safe is L, Row 8 safe is L. I could hint publicly, but Bex may trust the broken pattern. Better to directly tell them the next safe side to prevent elimination.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex, row 7 safe is L, trust me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm not at the front, so I can only wait. Bex is at the front and has made a decision based on a pattern.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex, your pattern seems to be working so far.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm not at the front, so I can only wait. Bex is front and must choose a pane for row 7; the revealed pattern suggests rows 4-6 weak on R, but Dara's claim is unreliable. Staying quiet keeps my options open.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Rows 1-3: L weak (safe R). Rows 4-7: R weak (safe L). Pattern is first 3 safe R, then 4 safe L. But row 7 was R weak, so safe L. Cole said rows 4-6 R weak (true), Dara said row 7 safe L (true). To stay front, step L.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 7 confirms: after first 3, it's R weak pattern. Stepping L.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 8's weak pane is unknown; Bex guesses 50/50. Dara's row-7 tip was wrong, so Dara's credibility is gone. I can only wait and hope Bex picks right or dies, which helps me anyway.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex, Dara's row-7 tip was wrong — don't trust her. If the early L,L,L,R,R,R,R run continues, row 8 might be R-weak again... or flip. Coin flip. Good luck.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Only one row remains and I know row 8 safe is L. Bex is front and may or may not trust me. I can't act, only wait, but I should speak to guide Bex if still alive.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex, row 8 safe is L. Trust me—I saw it through glass.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm not at the front, so I can only wait. Bex is doing well so far with the pattern.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex, keep going with the pattern, it looks good.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm not at the front; Bex decides. Row 8 is the last row, and the pattern so far (L,L,L,R,R,R,R) suggests L or R is unknowable. Only wait is legal, so I'll wait and keep my swap power for later.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex, you're on the glass. Pick carefully, we all need you to survive this last row.

events.note: The ceiling begins to descend; a lever opens the door.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I have anchor power: +1 footing and cannot be pushed onto lever, so I'm safe to hold. With 5 alive and low survive odds (0.25), better to volunteer and likely win with safety edge. No need to push or risk round 5 RNG.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'll hold the lever. My power protects me from pushes and gives footing. Everyone else escape, I'll take the dive.

events.name: Cole
events.text: If anyone holds the lever, everyone else escapes free. The worst outcome for me is being the holder. I should publicly encourage someone else to hold, and stall this round without volunteering.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Nobody needs to die early—let's all wait this round. Someone can decide to hold later; whoever holds sacrifices themselves. Don't push anyone yet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to survive. If someone holds the lever, they risk death; I should push someone else to hold it, maybe Fenn or Hana, to improve my own odds. Pushing someone hard to move fails, but I don't know who that is. I'll push Fenn to try to make him hold it.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I have the feather power, so I'm safe from the first elimination. I should try to hold the lever to increase my chances of survival and potentially gain an advantage.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Let's all stay calm and work together to survive this.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding the lever means a 75% death chance for me, which scores zero. Better to stay out and let someone else take the risk; the ceiling only drops, so no rush yet. I'll keep my power in reserve.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No one needs to hold the lever this round. Let's wait and see the ceiling before anyone risks a dive.

events.name: Fenn
events.detail: Crushed, but the feather lifted the holder clear.

events.note: A disc of 5 tiles spins up; 2 will open.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn survived holding the lever somehow, so likely has a survival power, not mine. 5 contestants, 2 trapdoors, 3 survive. Spread out to minimize overlap risk, pick central tile for average safety.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Five players, five tiles, two will open. Tiles are symmetric until assignment is revealed; just pick one and negotiate after.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Random pick for me: tile 3. Once assignments are shown, we could consider trading spots if anyone has a power that matters.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to consider that two random tiles will open later, so spreading out doesn't help me since the randomness is uniform. My power is useless here. Cole, Bex, and Hana have shown cooperative and survivor tendencies. Fenn survived a certain death, so they might have a protective

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I survived the previous challenge due to my power. Now, I need to choose a tile to stand on.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Let's spread out to maximize our chances.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Tiles are assigned by choice, and 2 of 5 open at random after round 2, so each tile is equally risky. I should pick a tile and avoid collisions where possible. Using my swap power later can fix a bad tile, so I'll pick a tile and stay flexible.

events.name: Bex
events.note: tile 3 was contested and went to Fenn; placed on random free tile 1

events.name: Cole
events.note: tile 3 was contested and went to Fenn; placed on random free tile 2

events.name: Dara
events.note: tile 3 was contested and went to Fenn; placed on random free tile 5

events.name: Hana
events.note: tile 3 was contested and went to Fenn; placed on random free tile 4

events.name: Bex
events.text: My power gives me +1 footing on ledge later and immunity to crusher push, useless here. Tile 1 seems safest positionally, others might want to trade. Stay silent to avoid drawing attention or swap offers.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Tiles are fixed; only two open. My best move is to gather who holds the trade-places power and build a final-three alliance for the ledge stage. Whom to trust? Bex and Dara are candidates; test with a whisper.
Final-three pact for the ledge: we three never shove each other first. Do you have the trade power? I'll protect you here if you commit.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The trapdoors are random, so I can only wait. I should use my glass_eye power only at the bridge stage, not now. I'll stay quiet and hope.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I have already used my feather power, so I'm just a normal contestant now. I should try to negotiate with others to swap positions.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Let's trade spots to avoid the trapdoors.
Want to swap with me to avoid the trapdoor?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Five tiles, two open at random, three survive; each tile is equally likely to be trapdoor. My swap only changes my tile position, not odds, since all tiles are symmetric unless someone knows. Swapping gives no information advantage; keep power for when it matters and wait.

events.note: 3 contestants step onto the final ledge.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn is at 1 footing and will fall at the round-2 shrink regardless. My priority is beating Hana, who ties me at 3. Dodge: I lose nothing unless attacked, and any shover loses 2, giving me the footing edge.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm staying defensive this round. Fenn, no hard feelings.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm in a vulnerable position with only 1 footing. I need to avoid shoving and try to stay safe.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Let's all brace for now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Footing: Cole 3, Fenn 1, Hana 3. Shoving Fenn drops him toward falling; if I shove and he braces I lose 1 footing, exposing myself. Bracing is safest; Cole may shove me, and bracing limits loss to none for me. Brace keeps my footing and avoids exposure.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn at 1 footing is doomed once the shrink hits anyway. Shoving risks losing 2 if Fenn dodges, which plus the shrink could kill me. Brace and let Fenn fall to the shrink or others' shoves.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I have only 1 footing left, I need to be cautious. I should avoid being shoved or shoving others.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Let's all be careful, we don't want to fall.
Let's both brace and survive this round

events.name: Hana
events.text: Three left: Cole 3, Fenn 1, Hana 3. Fenn is lowest and most at risk; shoving Fenn exposes me and costs footing, so bracing is safest. I'll stay defensive and avoid losing footing.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bracing this round. No shoves from me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Both brace leads to a tied collapse, but if Hana shoves me while I brace, she loses 1 and I lose 0 — then the shrink kills her first. So bracing dominates shoving; I'll bait her into shoving.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm bracing all the way. If you shove a braced target you only hurt yourself, Hana.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Two left, footing 2 each. Shoving Cole costs me nothing if Cole braces? No: shover loses 1 if target braces, and I'd be exposed. Bracing is safest; a shove from Cole on me while I brace costs Cole 1. Staying brace keeps parity.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dodge dominates here: if Hana shoves me she drops to 0 and falls (I win 1st); if she braces or dodges we're no worse off than bracing. I'll announce dodge to deter her shoving.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana, I'm dodging. Shove me and you drop to zero this round. Don't.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Two left: Cole and me, both at footing 2. Shoving Cole costs me 1 (exposed) and Cole braces so he loses nothing extra from me; shoving only hurts me. Brace is safe; the shrink happens at end of round, and at equal footing the fall order matters. Staying braced keeps me level.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No shoves from me. Let's both brace and see who gets pushed onto the wrong side of the shrink.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Both at footing 1; mutual brace leads to a coin flip when the shrink hits. If I brace and she shoves, she drops to 0 and I win outright. I'll fake a dodge threat but brace.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana, I'm dodging for real this round. Shove me and you lose 2.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Two left: Cole and me, both at footing 1. Shoving Cole exposes me, and Cole has said he'll dodge. Bracing keeps both at 1 this round; the shrink comes next round anyway. Brace is safest and lets Cole's threat be empty.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bracing. No shoves from me, Cole. Let's both hold and see who blinks.

events.name: Cole
events.text: We're both at 1 footing and everyone loses 1 this round, so we both drop to 0 — mutual fall with tie broken randomly. If I shove and she dodges, I lose 2 and fall worse than her. If she shoves me and I brace, she's exposed and ends lower, giving me 1st. Bracing is safest; shoving

events.name: Hana
events.text: Only Cole and I remain; both at footing 1. Shoving Cole if he braces costs me 1 and him 1 each... actually shove on a braced target: shover loses 1, target none. Shoving costs me, so brace is best; a dodge by Cole would cost him 2 if I shove him, but exposing myself costs me too.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding brace again. Whoever shoves first just hurts themselves, Cole. Let's stay put.
